query: What happens during an acid-base neutralization reaction?
title: Acid-Base Neutralization and Titration Reactions

scenes.title: When Opposites Meet
scenes.narration: Acids and bases represent opposite chemical extremes that neutralize one another when mixed in stoichiometric balance.
scenes.key_takeaway: Neutralization occurs when acids and bases react to cancel each other out.

scenes.title: The Fundamental Ionic Reaction
scenes.narration: At the microscopic level, acidic protons and alkaline hydroxide ions combine rapidly into pure water.
scenes.key_takeaway: Hydronium and hydroxide combine directly into water molecules.

scenes.title: Salt Formation and pH Shift
scenes.narration: Meanwhile, spectator ions combine to produce dissolved salt as the solution shifts toward neutral pH seven.
scenes.key_takeaway: Counter-ions form salt, while solution pH shifts toward neutral 7.

scenes.title: Titration and Analytical Precision
scenes.narration: Chemists employ neutralization reactions during volumetric titrations to determine unknown acid concentrations with high analytical precision.
scenes.key_takeaway: Titration uses neutralization to accurately calculate chemical concentrations.
